title: TRL Evidence Ledger
body:
Overview

This record belongs to the Technology Readiness and Maturation Database (public edition), a database that tracks evidence, unresolved risks, prototypes, and milestones for each technology as it matures toward operational use. TRL Evidence Ledger covers the following: collects every evidence item for a technology, grouped by readiness level, in one ledger. The record is written as a complete, usable file: it states what the entry is, how it is used, and what its limits are, and it carries a demo program that was genuinely executed at build time, with its output stored beside the code. Design targets only: labels in this record describe design targets for engineering work, never a claim of NASA, DARPA, or contractor qualification or approval.

How it works

A readiness record attaches evidence items to a readiness level, lists unresolved risks beside them, and advances a level only when its evidence checklist is complete and its risks are retired or accepted in writing. Applied to this record, the method means the following in practice: collects every evidence item for a technology, grouped by readiness level, in one ledger. The record sits at ladder rank simple in the teaching ladder, which runs simple, then compounded, then most complex, so a reader can start from the simpler records and work toward this one.

Worked example

The demo attaches evidence items to a readiness level and prints the level, evidence count, and open risks. The demo program prints:

Readiness level: TRL 1
Evidence items attached: 4
Unresolved risks: 0
Advance: False

Use and limits

A readiness level describes evidence held, not future success. A high level with thin evidence is recorded as a gap, never as maturity, and levels are design assessments, not claims of outside qualification. In practice, a reader can use this record to run the same check on their own tasks: follow the method, compare the result with the worked example, and record any difference with its evidence. The record is one of sixteen in this database, and it cross-links to related databases so the reader can continue from here without guessing where to look next.
